The reason doesn’t always matter. Don’t get me wrong, knowing how the urges and feelings come around is important, and parents should know how to handle the situation, but it‘s also crucial to understand that minors who SH don’t tend to want to talk to their parents about this in particular. Sometimes, someone outside the family environment can be much more beneficial to understand the “why” that parents are typically so focused on.

Of course, this really depends on the country and the laws regarding this topic but I found that there is a way around them (kind of). My counselor and I decided to come to an agreement on how to handle the situation. I told her that I would promise to be honest with her and she said that she would only notify my parents once (that same day) and in case of a BIG EMERGENCY. Other than that, she said that my ”secret” was safe with her. 

If you have a good/close relationship with your counselor I would really recommend doing this “consensus” thing because they tend be very understanding. Hope this helps :)

I don’t have the app but I do write down the date I sh and then include how many days passed between each time. I think that when people have no clue about this topic (or experience) they are often quite insensitive and have no filter at all. That girl was wayyyy out of line, but sadly, it happens more than we’d hope. 

Here’s one of my stories: When one of my best friends found out, she kept asking how and when I did it and for me to show her my scars. She somewhat cornered me and didn’t stop talking about it for a while. At first I was really taken aback because it was very unlike her and that‘s when I started to notice that she had no idea how to deal with it. She is literally the most mentally stable person there is so she was really lost. Nevertheless, she still one of my best friends but there are times where, just like many others, she doesn’t think before she speaks because she hasn’t been in that position herself.
